mainTopic: Whether פיגול intent spreads between paired loaves, combining half-כזית thoughts across עבודות, and a new משנה on one communal bread becoming טמא
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge to an earlier explanation of רבי יוסי. That challenge is a כל שכן. רבי יוחנן then gives a new reason: the פסוק treats the שתי הלחם as one body and also as two bodies. So intent that joins both loaves makes both פיגול, while intent about one loaf affects only that loaf. A ברייתא from רב תחליפא adds that the same מחלוקת applies to the breads of a תודה and to a מנחת מאפה. Next, a ברייתא teaches that half-כזית thoughts during שחיטה and during זריקה combine to make פיגול. רבא explains that this ברייתא follows the רבנן, while לוי's ברייתא, which says no עבודות combine, follows רבי. אביי questions the proof from רבי's ruling on the two lambs, and רבא בר רב חנן challenges אביי. אביי answers that a rabbinic decree is made only when a twin case of real פיגול exists, and the end of the משנה about מנחת חוטא supports this. Finally, a new משנה asks what happens when one of the two communal breads becomes טמא. רבי אלעזר limits the מחלוקת to טומאה that happened before the זריקה. רב פפא explains that the argument is about whether the ציץ makes eaten items acceptable, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: All the more so here, since the intent is about the offering itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a challenge begun earlier on the daf. If רבי יוסי says something becomes פיגול in a weaker case, then here, where the intent is about the offering itself, it should certainly become פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: [In that other case, רבי יוסי says] they become פיגול. Here, where he had intent about them in the offering itself, isn't it all the more so?
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a question that started before this section. It argues that an earlier explanation of רבי יוסי cannot be right, because a stronger case should obviously become פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is a כל שכן (all the more so). In the משנה (13a), רבי יוסי agrees that if the קומץ is taken with intent to burn the קומץ the next day, the שיריים (the remainder) become פיגול, even though the intent was not about the שיריים at all; it was about the קומץ. That is the weaker case. Here, in רב הונא's case, the intent is about part of the offering itself (one thigh), so all the more so the other thigh should become פיגול. רב הונא's explanation of רבי יוסי's view therefore seems to fall apart, and the גמרא will need a new reason.

keyTerms.meaning: They become פיגול, meaning invalid because of improper intent about when the offering will be eaten
All the more so; an argument from a weaker case to a stronger one
The offering (slaughtering) itself, as opposed to its leftovers
He had intent; the improper thought that can create פיגול

steps.confusionAlert: This section starts in the middle of a sentence. The first word, מיפגלי, is the end of a quote of רבי יוסי from the previous section. It is not a new statement.

phrases.english: they are rendered piggul;
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from just before this section, where רבי יוסי ruled that the remainder becomes פיגול.

phrases.english: here, where he had intent regarding them
in the offering itself,
is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא דְּחַשֵּׁיב בְּהוּ בִּזְבִיחָה גּוּפַהּ, לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge, begun earlier on the daf, against the previous explanation of רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier explanation of why רבי יוסי says פיגול does not spread from one loaf to the other
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כל שכן: רבי יוסי lets פיגול spread in a weaker case, so it should spread here too, where the intent touches the offering itself

steps.title: The פסוק made the loaves both one body and two bodies
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives a new reason for רבי יוסי. The two loaves are 'one body' because each one holds the other back, and 'two bodies' because each loaf is prepared separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן said: This is רבי יוסי's reason. The פסוק made them one body, and the פסוק made them two bodies. They are one body because they hold each other back. They are two bodies because the Torah said: this one is made by itself, and that one is made by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier explanation was knocked down, so רבי יוחנן offers a completely new reason for רבי יוסי's view about the two loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two loaves have a double identity. They are 'one body' because neither loaf is valid without the other (מעכבי אהדדי). They are also 'two bodies' because the Torah requires each loaf to be prepared on its own. This double identity is what lets רבי יוסי treat them sometimes as one unit and sometimes as two separate things.

keyTerms.meaning: One body; treated as a single unit
Two bodies; treated as two separate items
They hold each other back; one is invalid without the other
The Merciful One; a name for ה׳ as the One who gave the Torah
It is made by itself, separately

steps.whyThisMatters: This 'one body and two bodies' idea becomes the key to רבי יוסי's whole position. The next step builds directly on it.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yochanan said:
This is the reason of Rabbi Yosei:
The verse made them one body,
and the verse made them two bodies;
one body — in that they hold each other back;
two bodies — as the Merciful One said:
this one is made by itself
and that one is made by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that was rejected in step 1 with a new reason
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reasoning that replaces the rejected explanation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי's view was explained in a way that clashed with his other ruling (the כל שכן)
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי's view rests on the double identity of the loaves: one body and also two bodies

steps.title: Joined intent makes both פיגול; separate intent affects only one
steps.stepSummary: Applying the double identity: if the intent covers both loaves together, both become פיגול. If it covers only one loaf, only that loaf becomes פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he mixed them, they are mixed, because the פסוק made them one body. If he split them, they are split, because the פסוק made them two bodies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יוחנן's 'one body and two bodies' reason works in practice for פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן's intent decides which identity counts. If he thinks about eating a כזית from both loaves together, he joins them, and the 'one body' side makes both loaves פיגול. If he thinks about only one loaf, he separates them, and the 'two bodies' side keeps the other loaf from becoming פיגול. This also explains why the כל שכן from step 1 is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: He mixed (joined) them; his intent covered both loaves together
They are mixed; treated as one unit
He split them; his intent covered only one loaf
They are split; treated as separate

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי, the two loaves are both one body and two bodies. Intent that joins them makes both פיגול. Intent about only one loaf makes only that loaf פיגול.

phrases.english: If he mixed them — they are mixed,
phrases.notes: 'Mixed' means his intent was to eat a כזית from both loaves together, not that he physically mixed them.

phrases.english: since the verse made them one body;
if he split them, they are split,
since the verse made them two bodies.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָרְבִינְהוּ – מִתְעָרְבִין, דְּהַכָּתוּב עֲשָׂאָן גּוּף אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי יוחנן's reason from step 2 to the actual פיגול ruling
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי יוסי, whether פיגול spreads depends on whether the intent joined the loaves or separated them

steps.title: Does the same rule apply to תודה breads and מנחת מאפה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks whether this rule also applies to the breads of a thanks offering and to a baked meal offering. Both are made of different kinds of bread that come together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן asked: If he had פיגול intent about the breads of a תודה, what is the law? About a מנחת מאפה, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן raises a new question. He wants to know whether the 'one loaf does not spread to the other' idea applies to other offerings made of more than one kind of bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The breads of a תודה come in different types, and a מנחת מאפה can be made as חלות or רקיקין. The question is whether intent about one type spreads to the other types. Put another way, the question is whether the same מחלוקת between רבי יוסי and the חכמים applies there too.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a real question (a dilemma) whose answer he did not know
The breads brought together with a thanks offering
A baked meal offering, made as loaves or as wafers
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan asked:
If he had piggul intent regarding the breads of a thanks offering, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means intent about one type of the תודה breads: does it spread to the other types?

phrases.english: Regarding a baked meal offering, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: פִּיגֵּל בְּלַחְמֵי תוֹדָה מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the rule for שתי הלחם and asks whether it extends to other offerings with more than one kind of bread
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether פיגול intent about one type of bread in a תודה or a מנחת מאפה spreads to the other types, the same way as in the משנה's case of the two loaves

steps.title: A ברייתא from ארץ ישראל: the same applies there
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא from ארץ ישראל quotes a ברייתא saying the same rule and the same מחלוקת apply to תודה breads and to מנחת מאפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב תחליפא from the West taught him: And so you say about the breads of a תודה, and so you say about a מנחת מאפה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב תחליפא answers רבי יוחנן's question by quoting a ברייתא. It says these cases follow the same law as the two loaves in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'and so you say' mean the same מחלוקת between רבי יוסי and the חכמים applies here. According to רבי יוסי, intent about one type of bread does not automatically spread to the other types. According to the חכמים, it does.

keyTerms.meaning: The West; refers to ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל
And so you say; the same law applies to this case too
He taught him (a ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת of רבי יוסי and the חכמים about the two loaves also applies to תודה breads and to מנחת מאפה.

phrases.english: Rav Tachlifa from the West taught him:
phrases.notes: 'The West' means ארץ ישראל. רב תחליפא is quoting a ברייתא.

phrases.english: And so you say regarding the breads of a thanks offering,
and so you say regarding a baked meal offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא לֵיהּ רַב תַּחְלִיפָא מִמַּעְרְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's question from step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא states that the same law, including the same מחלוקת, applies to תודה breads and to מנחת מאפה

steps.title: Half a כזית at שחיטה plus half at זריקה combine to make פיגול
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a half-כזית thought at שחיטה and a half-כזית thought at זריקה add up to make the offering פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If during the slaughter he planned to eat half an olive-size, and during the sprinkling he planned to eat another half an olive-size, the offering is פיגול, because thoughts during שחיטה and זריקה add up together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא. Two small wrong thoughts, each only half the needed amount, are combined to make פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally פיגול needs a thought about a full כזית. Here each thought is only half a כזית, but they were made during two different עבודות. The ברייתא says the two עבודות join, so together they reach a full כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: Half an olive-size, half the amount needed for פיגול
Slaughtering the animal
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
They combine, they add up together

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
At the time of slaughter he intended
to eat half an olive-bulk,
and at the time of sprinkling he intended
to eat half an olive-bulk, it is piggul,
because slaughter and sprinkling combine.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: combining thoughts across different עבודות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Half-כזית thoughts at שחיטה and at זריקה combine to make פיגול.

steps.title: First view: only slaughter and sprinkling combine, because both permit the offering
steps.stepSummary: One version says only שחיטה and זריקה combine, since both are מתירין; קבלה and הולכה do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: slaughter and sprinkling, since both of them make the offering permitted, yes, they combine. Collecting the blood and carrying it, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how far the ברייתא's rule goes. The first version limits it to שחיטה and זריקה only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שחיטה and זריקה are both acts that make the offering permitted (מתירין). That shared role is why they can join. קבלה and הולכה are not מתירין, so thoughts during them do not add up.

keyTerms.meaning: Acts that make the offering permitted to eat or offer
Collecting the blood in a holy vessel
Carrying the blood to the מזבח

phrases.english: Some say: slaughter and sprinkling,
since both of them are permitting acts, yes, they combine,
collection and carrying, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: שְׁחִיטָה וּזְרִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא's rule to the two מתירין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only שחיטה and זריקה combine; קבלה and הולכה do not.

steps.title: Second view: if far-apart acts combine, close acts surely do
steps.stepSummary: Another version says: if שחיטה and זריקה, which are far apart, combine, then קבלה and הולכה, which are close together, certainly combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: if those acts that are far apart combine, all the more so these acts that are close together combine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version that widens the rule. It uses a כל שכן to include קבלה and הולכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version looks at distance, not at being מתירין. שחיטה is the first עבודה and זריקה is the last, so they are far apart. קבלה and הולכה come right after each other, so if far acts join, close acts should join even more.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so, a stronger case
Which are far apart
Which are close together

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. The first says only the מתירין combine. The second says all four combine, because the close acts are an even stronger case.

phrases.english: And some say:
those that are far apart combine,
phrases.notes: These are שחיטה and זריקה, the first and last עבודות.

phrases.english: and all the more so these that are close together.
phrases.notes: These are קבלה and הולכה, which come right after each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: הָנָךְ דִּמְרַחֲקָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reading of how far the ברייתא's rule reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All four עבודות combine, by a כל שכן from שחיטה and זריקה.

steps.title: לוי's ברייתא says none of the four עבודות combine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from לוי, who teaches that none of the four עבודות, not even שחיטה and זריקה, combine for פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But לוי teaches: Four services do not combine for פיגול: slaughter and sprinkling, collecting and carrying!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא of step 6. Another ברייתא, taught by לוי, says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said שחיטה and זריקה combine. לוי lists שחיטה and זריקה among the four עבודות that do not combine. The two ברייתות clash directly.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? Opens a challenge
The services done with an offering

phrases.english: Is that so?
But Levi teaches:
Four services do not combine to make piggul:
slaughter and sprinkling, collection and carrying!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא תָּנֵי לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא of step 6 from a conflicting ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא that שחיטה and זריקה combine for פיגול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: לוי's ברייתא says plainly that שחיטה and זריקה do not combine.

steps.title: רבא: the two ברייתות follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that לוי's ברייתא follows רבי, and the first ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is not difficult. This one follows רבי, and that one follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא solves the clash by saying the two ברייתות reflect a real מחלוקת between תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither ברייתא is wrong. לוי's ruling that nothing combines matches רבי. The ruling that שחיטה and זריקה combine matches the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult, there is an answer
This one ... that one, splitting two sources

phrases.english: Rava said: It is not difficult:
this one is Rabbi, that one is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: לוי's teaching follows רבי; the first ברייתא, where they combine, follows the רבנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא רַבִּי, הָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the two sources to different תנאים (רבי vs. רבנן).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: They reflect a מחלוקת: רבי holds the עבודות do not combine, the רבנן hold they do.

steps.title: Proof: רבי rules the שבועות lambs stay כשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves רבי's view from a ברייתא: two lambs slaughtered, each with a half-כזית thought about the loaf, and רבי says the offering is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: One who slaughters the lamb planning to eat half an olive-size from this loaf, and likewise the other lamb planning to eat half an olive-size from this loaf, רבי says: I say that this is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבא by showing a ברייתא where רבי refuses to combine two half thoughts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two lambs of שבועות are slaughtered separately, each with only a half-כזית wrong thought. If the thoughts added up, it would be פיגול. רבי says it is כשר, so for him thoughts during separate permitting acts do not combine, just like לוי's ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A lamb, here one of the two lambs of שבועות
A loaf, here one of the שתי הלחם
Its fellow, the second lamb
Valid

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's answer: the רבנן hold that half-כזית thoughts during שחיטה and זריקה combine to make פיגול, while לוי's ברייתא follows רבי, who rules the lambs כשר. The next step shows that אביי questions whether this ruling of רבי really proves the point.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
One who slaughters the lamb
to eat half an olive-bulk from this loaf,
and likewise the other lamb,
to eat half an olive-bulk from this loaf,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אוֹמֵר אֲנִי שֶׁזֶּה כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: Rabbi says: I say that this is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַכֶּבֶשׂ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's answer by showing that רבי does not combine thoughts.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that רבי holds thoughts in separate עבודות do not combine.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the two lambs of שבועות, where רבי rules the offering כשר.

steps.title: אביי: maybe רבי only spoke about half a permitting factor
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof from the two lambs. That case had only half a מתיר, so it tells us nothing about a whole מתיר with half a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You heard רבי rule this way about half a מתיר and half a כזית. Did you ever hear him say it about a whole מתיר and half a כזית?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the proof from Step 11. He says the case there was too weak to prove anything about a stronger case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the two-lambs case each half-כזית thought happened during only one lamb, so only half of the מתיר. אביי says רבי called it כשר because both parts were halves. If the thought covered the whole מתיר and only the amount was half a כזית, רבי might agree it combines into פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: The permitting factor: the part of the offering that makes the rest allowed (here, the two lambs)
Half of the permitting factor, such as only one of the two lambs
The entire permitting factor
Half the eating-measure, meaning half a כַּזַּיִת

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different 'halves' here. One is half of the action (one lamb out of two). The other is half of the amount (half a כזית). Keep them separate.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Granted, you heard Rabbi [rule it is valid]
where it is half a permitting factor and half an eating-measure;
phrases.notes: Half a permitting factor means one lamb out of the two. Half an eating-measure means half a כזית of the loaf.

phrases.english: but a whole permitting factor and half an eating-measure,
did you hear him [say that]?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 11 by limiting רבי's ruling to a narrower case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that רבי holds no combining at all, even for שחיטה and זריקה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two-lambs case had only half a מתיר, so it cannot show what רבי holds when the whole מתיר is involved.

steps.title: If so, רבי should have decreed against the weaker case
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב חנן challenges אביי: if רבי makes a whole מתיר with half a כזית into פיגול, he should at least disqualify the half-מתיר case as a גזירה, not call it fully כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב חנן said to אביי: If רבי holds that a whole מתיר with half a כזית is פיגול, he should decree against half a מתיר with half a כזית, so people do not mix it up with the whole-מתיר case. After all, רבי יוסי makes decrees like this, and so do the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר רב חנן attacks אביי's answer. He also announces two examples, which the גמרא will spell out in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11 רבי said the offering is fully כשר. If the whole-מתיר case were real פיגול, we would expect him to at least disqualify the very similar half-מתיר case by rabbinic decree. Since he said כשר with no decree, it seems he does not hold even the whole-מתיר case is פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: To make a rabbinic decree (גְּזֵירָה)
Because of; out of concern that it will be confused with
He decrees / they decree

steps.whyThisMatters: This brings in a new tool: a case that is not פיגול by Torah law can still be made פסול by the Sages, so people do not confuse it with a real פיגול case.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Ḥanan said to Abaye:
But if Rabbi holds
[that] a whole permitting factor and half an eating-measure [makes piggul],
let him decree against half a permitting factor and half an eating-measure
because of a whole permitting factor and half an eating-measure,
for Rabbi Yosei decrees [in such cases]
and the Rabbis decree!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי כּוּלּוֹ מַתִּיר וַחֲצִי אֲכִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's rejection in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's idea that רבי might hold a whole מתיר with half a כזית is פיגול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were so, רבי should have made a גזירה and disqualified the half-מתיר case, just as רבי יוסי and the רבנן make such decrees elsewhere. Instead he called it fully כשר.

steps.title: Proof that רבי יוסי makes such a decree
steps.stepSummary: The משנה about burning the לבונה tomorrow: רבי יוסי says פסול but no כרת. This shows a rabbinic disqualification made because of the real פיגול case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי decrees, as the משנה teaches: If he intended to burn the לבונה tomorrow, רבי יוסי says it is פסול but there is no כרת. The חכמים say it is פיגול and there is כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the first example promised in Step 13 by quoting a משנה with רבי יוסי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, a thought about the לבונה alone is not real פיגול, so there is no כרת. Even so, he does not call the מנחה כשר but פסול. That is a decree made so it is not confused with a thought about the קומץ, which is real פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: Frankincense placed on the מנחה and burned on the altar
To burn on the altar
Invalid, but without the כָּרֵת punishment of פיגול
Spiritual cutting-off, the punishment for eating real פיגול

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei decrees, as we learned [in a mishna]:
[If he took the handful intending] to burn its frankincense tomorrow,
Rabbi Yosei says:
it is invalid, but there is no karet for it;
and the Sages say:
it is piggul and one is liable to karet for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי גָּזַר, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim in Step 13 that רבי יוסי makes such decrees.
steps.raayaObject: That Sages disqualify a non-פיגול case by decree because it resembles real פיגול
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on 13a: לְהַקְטִיר לְבוֹנָתָהּ לְמָחָר, רבי יוסי says פסול with no כרת

steps.title: Proof that the רבנן also make such a decree
steps.stepSummary: The משנה about a פיגול thought during only the קומץ or only the לבונה: the חכמים say no כרת, but they do not call it כשר. This shows a rabbinic disqualification.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן also decree, as the משנה teaches: If he had a פיגול thought during the burning of the קומץ but not the לבונה, or the לבונה but not the קומץ, רבי מאיר says it is פיגול with כרת. The חכמים say there is no כרת unless he had the thought during the whole מתיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the second example from Step 13, showing that the רבנן also make this kind of decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קומץ and the לבונה together are the full מתיר of a מנחה. The חכמים say a thought during only half of it brings no כרת, but they only remove the כרת and do not say the מנחה is כשר. So they treat it as פסול by rabbinic decree because of the whole-מתיר case. This is exactly the kind of decree רבא בר רב חנן expected from רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful of flour taken from a מנחה and burned on the altar
He had a פיגול thought, an improper intent about time
The entire permitting factor (here, both the קומץ and the לבונה)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא בר רב חנן's point: if רבי held that a whole מתיר with half a כזית is פיגול, he should have disqualified the half-מתיר case by decree, as רבי יוסי and the רבנן do. Since he called it fully כשר, אביי's limit on רבי's view is under pressure.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis also decree, as we learned [in a mishna]:
If he had a piggul thought during the handful but not the frankincense,
or during the frankincense but not the handful,
Rabbi Meir says:
it is piggul and one is liable to karet for it;
and the Sages say:
there is no karet for it
unless he has the piggul thought during the entire permitting factor.
phrases.notes: The handful and the frankincense together are what permit the מנחה, so both together make up the whole permitting factor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן נָמֵי גָּזְרִי, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second source promised in Step 13, alongside רבי יוסי in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן disqualify a half-מתיר case by decree because of the whole-מתיר case
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on 16a: פיגל בקומץ ולא בלבונה, where the חכמים say no כרת unless the thought covers כל המתיר

steps.title: אביי explains the decrees in the two משניות
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the two משניות cannot be compared. In each one, the decree is based on a twin case where the same act really is full פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: How can you compare? Granted, there, רבי יוסי decreed about the handful of frankincense because of the handful of the meal offering. The Rabbis decreed about the handful because of the handful of the sinner's meal offering, and about frankincense because of the frankincense brought in the bowls.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the proofs from steps 14 and 15. He explains that each rabbinic disqualification there is based on a closely matching case where the same act truly makes the offering פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי disqualifies a thought about burning the לבונה tomorrow because a thought about burning the קומץ of the מנחה tomorrow is real פיגול. The חכמים disqualify a thought during only the קומץ because in a מנחת חוטא, which has no לבונה, the קומץ alone is the whole מתיר. They disqualify a thought during only the לבונה because with the לחם הפנים, the לבונה in the bowls is the whole מתיר.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejects a comparison)
Made a rabbinic decree
Because of; out of concern for (a similar case)
A sinner's meal offering, which has no לבונה
The bowls of לבונה that come with the לחם הפנים

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not denying that these are rabbinic disqualifications. He agrees they are. His point is that each one copies a real twin case, so they do not prove a decree is needed in every situation.

phrases.english: He said to him: How can these be compared?
phrases.notes: אביי is answering רבא בר רב חנן.

phrases.english: Granted, there,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה from step 14 about burning the לבונה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei decreed about the handful of frankincense
because of the handful of the meal offering.
The Rabbis decreed about the handful
phrases.notes: This is the משנה from step 15.

phrases.english: because of the handful of the sinner's meal offering,
and about frankincense because of frankincense
that comes in the bowls.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה הכי השתא בשלמא התם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proofs brought in steps 14 and 15 for רבא בר רב חנן's challenge.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proofs from the two משניות about the קומץ and the לבונה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Those decrees are each based on a twin case where the same act is truly full פיגול, so they do not show a decree must exist in every case.

steps.title: The same pattern with the lambs and the bowls
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds that the rabbinic disqualifications for one of the two lambs and for one of the two bowls follow the same pattern: one is decreed because of the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: With the lambs too, one lamb is decreed because of its fellow lamb. With a bowl, it is decreed because of its fellow bowl.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues his answer. He shows that other known rabbinic disqualifications are also based on a matching real case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the two lambs of שבועות, a פיגול thought while slaughtering only one lamb is disqualified because the same thought during both lambs would be real פיגול. The same is true for burning one of the two bowls of לבונה with the לחם הפנים. Each decree has a direct twin case, and this is the pattern אביי says the proofs follow.

keyTerms.meaning: The two lambs that come with the שתי הלחם on שבועות
The other lamb of the pair
A single bowl of לבונה

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the rabbinic disqualifications in these cases are each modeled on a matching case of real פיגול: a handful because of another handful, לבונה because of לבונה, a lamb because of its fellow lamb, and a bowl because of its fellow bowl.

phrases.english: With the lambs as well,
phrases.notes: These are the two lambs of שבועות, discussed in a משנה later (16a).

phrases.english: one lamb is decreed because of its fellow lamb.
A bowl is decreed because of its fellow bowl.

steps.triggerLanguage: כבשים נמי כבש אטו כבש חבירו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the principle from step 16 to the cases of the lambs and the bowls.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that each rabbinic decree rests on a closely matching real case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Rabbinic disqualifications show that רבי should decree on any case that resembles פיגול.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each known decree is modeled on a direct twin case: a lamb because of its fellow lamb, and a bowl because of its fellow bowl.

steps.title: No real case of half a permitting factor and half a כזית exists, so there is nothing to decree from
steps.stepSummary: אביי concludes his answer to רבא בר רב חנן: a גזירה needs a real twin case to be based on, and half a מתיר with half a כזית never makes anything real פיגול anywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, is there anywhere at all a case of half a permitting factor and half a כזית that is real פיגול, so that רבי should get up and decree because of it?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי closes his answer to the question of step 13. He explains why רבי calls the half-מתיר, half-כזית case fully כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 16-17, every rabbinic disqualification was based on a twin case that really is פיגול. Here, half a מתיר together with half a כזית is never real פיגול in any case. So there is nothing to make a decree from, and the offering stays כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Half of the permitting factor, such as only one of the two lambs
Half of the minimum amount of eating, meaning half a כזית
To make a rabbinic decree (גזירה)
Anywhere at all, in general

steps.whatToRemember: A rabbinic פסול for פיגול thoughts is made only when the same kind of act is real פיגול in a twin case. With no twin case, there is no decree.

phrases.english: But here,
is there half a permitting factor
and half an eating anywhere at all,
phrases.notes: "Half an eating" means a thought about eating only half a כזית.

phrases.english: that he should get up and decree?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכָא, מִי אִיכָּא חֲצִי מַתִּיר וַחֲצִי אֲכִילָה בְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer after showing that the other decrees all have twin cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: no twin case of real פיגול exists
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי should at least disqualify the half-מתיר case by rabbinic decree.
steps.terutzMaskana: A decree needs a similar real פיגול case, and here none exists, so it is fully כשר.

steps.title: Support from the end of the משנה about the sinner's meal offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says אביי's explanation makes sense, and quotes the end of the משנה: the חכמים agree that a פיגול thought on the קומץ of a מנחת חוטא or מנחת קנאות is real פיגול with כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that this is the reason of the חכמים, because the end of the משנה teaches: the חכמים agree with רבי מאיר that for a מנחת חוטא and a מנחת קנאות, a פיגול thought during the קומץ makes it פיגול with כרת, because the קומץ is the only מתיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for אביי's idea. Here it only quotes the source; the next step explains how it proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two מנחות have no לבונה, so the קומץ alone is the whole מתיר. That makes them the twin case for the regular מנחה, where a thought during only the קומץ is rabbinically פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable, it makes sense
The latter clause of a משנה
The meal offering a poor sinner brings instead of an animal
The meal offering of jealousy brought for a סוטה
The handful of flour taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable
that the reason of the Rabbis is because of this,
phrases.notes: "This" means אביי's idea: they decree only because a similar case is real פיגול.

phrases.english: for it teaches in the latter clause:
The Sages agree with Rabbi Meir
regarding the sinner's meal offering and the meal offering of jealousy
that if he had a פיגול thought during the handful, it is פיגול,
and one is liable to כרת for it,
since the handful is the permitting factor.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּטַעְמָא דְּרַבָּנַן מִשּׁוּם הָכִי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings textual support for אביי's principle from steps 16-18.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that the חכמים' rabbinic פסול is based on a similar case that is real פיגול
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה about מנחת חוטא and מנחת קנאות

steps.title: Why the משנה needed to say the obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה states something so obvious, and answers that it is teaching the reason for the rabbinic פסול in a regular מנחה: the similar מנחת חוטא case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the משנה need to teach this at all? It is obvious, since there is no other מתיר. Rather, it must be teaching us that the reason for the ruling about the קומץ in a regular מנחה is that the קומץ of a מנחת חוטא is similar to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the quote from step 19 proves the point. It asks why the משנה bothers saying something obvious and finds a hidden lesson in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a מנחת חוטא has only the קומץ as its מתיר, of course it is real פיגול, so the line seems unneeded. The משנה says it to show why the חכמים disqualify a regular מנחה when the thought was only during the קומץ: it looks like the מנחת חוטא case. This confirms אביי's rule that a decree needs a twin case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
This is what it teaches us
Another permitting factor
It resembles it

steps.whatToRemember: The line about מנחת חוטא is not extra. It shows that the חכמים' rabbinic פסול on a regular מנחה comes from its resemblance to a real פיגול case.

phrases.english: Why do I need to teach this at all?
It is obvious, is there any other permitting factor?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן,
phrases.english: Rather, is it not that this is what it teaches us,
that the reason for the handful ruling
phrases.notes: This is the rule from step 15: in a regular מנחה, a thought during only the קומץ makes it פסול but without כרת.

phrases.english: is because there is the handful of the sinner's meal offering
which resembles it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לְמָה לִי לְמִיתְנָא כְּלָל? פְּשִׁיטָא, מִי אִיכָּא מַתִּיר אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the quote in step 19 supports אביי.
steps.raayaObject: The rabbinic פסול for a thought during only the קומץ in a regular מנחה is based on the similar מנחת חוטא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The apparently unneeded line in the סיפא of the משנה

steps.title: New משנה: one of the two communal breads becomes impure
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if one of the שתי הלחם or one of the two rows of לחם הפנים becomes טמא, רבי יהודה says both are burned because a קרבן ציבור is not divided; the חכמים say the impure one is burned and the pure one is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of the loaves or one of the rows became impure, רבי יהודה says: both go to be burned, because a communal offering is not split. The חכמים say: the impure one stays impure, and the pure one is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. It asks what happens to a pair of communal breads when only one of them becomes טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה sees the pair as one unit, so if part is unfit, all of it is unfit. The חכמים treat each one on its own: only the impure one is lost. This connects to the earlier theme of how one half of a pair affects the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Loaves; here the two loaves (שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם) brought on שבועות
Rows; here the two rows of the לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים
The place where disqualified offerings are burned
A communal offering, brought for all of כלל ישראל
Divided, split into parts

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not saying the pure loaf became טמא. It is still pure, but he holds it is burned anyway because a communal offering cannot be half fit and half unfit.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If one of the loaves became impure,
phrases.notes: These are the two loaves brought on שבועות.

phrases.english: or one of the rows,
phrases.notes: These are the two rows of the לחם הפנים on the שולחן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Both must go out to the place of burning,
since a communal offering is not divided.
And the Sages say:
The impure one remains in its impurity
and the pure one shall be eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נִטְמֵאת אַחַת מִן הַחַלּוֹת, אוֹ אֶחָד מִן הַסְּדָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: if one of a pair of communal breads becomes טמא, both are burned. חכמים: only the impure one is burned, and the pure one is eaten.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר limits the argument to before the sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the argument in the משנה is only when the loaf became טמא before the זריקה. After the זריקה, everyone agrees: the impure loaf stays impure and the pure one is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: רבי אלעזר says: The argument is only when the loaf became impure before the sprinkling of the blood. But if it became impure after the sprinkling, everyone agrees that the impure one stays impure and the pure one is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the new משנה. רבי אלעזר tells us exactly when the argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זריקה of the lambs' blood is what makes the loaves allowed to be eaten. If a loaf becomes טמא after the זריקה, both loaves were already allowed, so even רבי יהודה agrees the pure one is eaten. The argument only exists when the טומאה came before the זריקה, while the loaves still needed the זריקה to permit them.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
An argument or dispute between sages
Sprinkling the blood of the קרבן on the מזבח. Here it is the act that permits the loaves to be eaten
Everyone agrees
Ritually impure / ritually pure

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יהודה says to burn the pure loaf in every case. According to רבי אלעזר, after the זריקה even רבי יהודה lets the pure loaf be eaten.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Elazar says:
The dispute is when it happened before the sprinkling,
phrases.notes: This is the sprinkling of the lambs' blood. That sprinkling is what allows the loaves to be eaten.

phrases.english: but after the sprinkling,
everyone agrees
the impure one stays in its impurity
and the pure one shall be eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מַחְלוֹקֶת לִפְנֵי זְרִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה from step 21 and limits the case of the argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים applies only to טומאה before the זריקה. After the זריקה, all agree the pure loaf is eaten.

steps.title: What is the argument before the sprinkling about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle the two sides disagree about when the loaf became טמא before the זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And before the sprinkling, about what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question to find the root of the argument. This line sets up רב פפא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know the argument is only before the זריקה. The גמרא wants the underlying reason that makes one side burn both loaves and the other side eat the pure one.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? A question looking for the root of an argument

phrases.english: And before the sprinkling,
about what do they disagree?

steps.title: רב פפא: they argue about whether the frontplate covers eaten items
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the argument is about whether the ציץ makes a טמא offering acceptable even for parts that are eaten (אכילות).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: They disagree about whether the frontplate makes things acceptable for items that are eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question from the last step. He says the argument comes down to how far the power of the ציץ reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ, the gold plate on the כהן גדול's forehead, makes a קרבן acceptable even though something became טמא. Everyone agrees it works for parts offered on the מזבח. The question is whether it also works for parts that are eaten, like these loaves. That decides whether the זריקה can still permit the pure loaf.

keyTerms.meaning: The gold frontplate worn on the כהן גדול's forehead
Makes acceptable. Here it means fixing the problem of טומאה so the קרבן still works
Items that are eaten, as opposed to parts burned on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the argument about the loaves to a big general question in קדשים: does the ציץ help for eaten parts of a קרבן, or only for what goes on the מזבח?
